free_tier.stated: RUB 190 per month from the vendor's own page title, which states that VPS/VDS servers start at RUB 190 with hourly billing. The plan table itself is a JavaScript calculator that renders only a loading placeholder to a text extractor, so the shape comes from the index row: 5 GB NVMe, 1 GB RAM, 1 core at 2.3 GHz, 0.2 TB traffic on a 50 Mbit/s port, Moscow or Novosibirsk. The page states three plan lines (budget, standard, storage) and a 50 Mbit/s ceiling on the budget line against up to 250 Mbit/s on the other two.

egress.terms: no byte allowance stated on the page read; the budget line is capped at 50 Mbit/s, the other two at 250 Mbit/s

interface_detail: inferred from the tooling the provider documents; not probed
tooling: browser control panel with VNC, ISO mount, firewall rules and resource resize; no API documented on the page read
chaining: RUB 190 with hourly billing and a Moscow and a Novosibirsk location is the cheapest hourly Russian box, which makes it a candidate for short-lived jobs that must egress from inside Russia

limits.value: The budget line is capped at 50 Mbit/s and the page states no byte allowance, so throughput is the wall on the cheap plan; the index row's 0.2 TB is a rendering of the same 50 Mbit/s port, not a separate meter.
